title: The UX of AI: Making AI-Powered Apps Your Users Don't Hate - Kathryn Grayson Nanz, Progress Software
talk_summary: A UX/design talk about how to present AI features to end users, organized around five pillars: trust, clarity, control, transparency, and meaningful benefit.

takeaways.technique: Show an action plan and require approval before an agent acts
takeaways.what_they_do: Agentic tools display the list of steps they will take and ask for confirmation before starting, with settings to auto-approve repeated flows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: show an action plan to the user and allow them to approve it before the agent begins work

takeaways.what_they_do: Give users a big, obvious emergency brake to halt generation or an agentic workflow at any point, not buried in a menu.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a clear and prominent emergency brake that they can slam to bring everything to a halt

takeaways.technique: Checkpoints and granular rollback of agent output
takeaways.what_they_do: Provide undo/redo and save states so users can revert part of an AI's work without discarding everything, and make targeted adjustments instead of full retries.

takeaways.technique: Cite sources / show reasoning trail for verification
takeaways.what_they_do: Attach references and expose chain-of-thought so users can validate output and pinpoint where it went wrong.
takeaways.evidence_quote: By citing the references in an AI-generated response and linking users back directly to the source material

takeaways.technique: Templates, examples, and guided workflows instead of a blank box
takeaways.what_they_do: Provide suggested prompts, templates, and worked examples so users don't need AI literacy to get good output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can help them by providing examples, templates, suggested prompts, and guided workflows that demonstrate what success looks like

takeaways.technique: Show estimated cost/time before committing to an action
takeaways.what_they_do: Before approving an agent action, show a rough estimate of time and money/tokens so users can revise the request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they also need to know how much time something is going to take and what it's going to cost them in money or tokens
